verdict.rationale: First-party docs confirm Ubuntu ships built-in accessibility tooling, including dedicated 'Get started with the screen reader' and 'Read the screen aloud' guides, showing switchers have a documented path to onboard with these tools. However, missing for 10: independent/hands-on corroboration of screen reader usability, coverage of other accessibility features (magnifier, high-contrast, keyboard navigation) beyond the screen reader, and any switcher-specific onboarding narrative.
